summary: Syntactically valid and contains a reasonably complete simulation engine, but main() does nothing, so no simulation runs or outputs are produced. There is a logic issue with compliance averaging, some redundant pass statements and unused imports, and a potential performance hotspot in the small-world rewiring.

issues.description: main() is empty and the program does not run the simulation or emit any results when executed.
issues.location: main() function and global call at end of file
issues.solution: Implement main() to instantiate Simulation with default or parsed parameters, call sim.run(), and print or save the results (e.g., print JSON to stdout).

issues.description: Compliance rate averaging includes days with no mandated visits as 0.0, biasing the average downward.
issues.location: Simulation.step (appending to compliance_rate_in_mandated_areas) and Simulation.evaluate (computing average)
issues.solution: Append None when no mandated visits occur on a day and compute the average only across non-None days. Alternatively, track both masked and total mandated visits cumulatively and compute the ratio at evaluation.

issues.description: Small-world network rewiring selects candidates with an O(n) scan per edge, leading to O(n^2) behavior for large n.
issues.solution: Use a bounded random-attempt loop to sample new_j not in neighbors[i], or maintain a complement set for faster selection.

issues.description: Unused imports and variables (argparse, json, DATA_DIR) present.
issues.location: Top of file (imports) and DATA_DIR constant
issues.solution: Remove unused imports and variables, or integrate them (e.g., use argparse to accept parameters in main()).

issues.description: Redundant pass statements inside functions and class bodies before actual logic can be confusing, though harmless.
issues.location: Multiple functions and class bodies (e.g., clamp01, sigmoid, class Person, etc.)
issues.solution: Remove the redundant pass statements where executable logic follows immediately.

issues.description: Fatigue dynamics use fixed deltas and do not reference the configured fatigue_rate except as a decision weight, which may be inconsistent with user expectations.
issues.solution: Scale fatigue delta by a parameter, or document the intended separation between fatigue accumulation dynamics and decision weighting.
